title: Grand finale: assemble a solution from your own functions
idea: GUIDED FINALE. Decompose a word problem into helpers you write, then compose them — the full engineering loop.
problem: Compute the area of a border: outer square area minus inner square area. Use area(side) for both (outer 5, inner 3 -> 25 - 9 = 16).

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: border area = outer area - inner area, each a square. OUTPUT is...
options: One number: the leftover border area
exercises.explanation: Output is the difference of two areas. We'll compute each with a helper, then subtract.

exercises.prompt: How does decomposing into area(side) help here?
options: We write the square-area logic ONCE and call it twice
exercises.explanation: One helper, two calls (outer and inner). Decomposition + composition — the heart of this course.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand: outer side 5 -> area 25; inner side 3 -> area 9. Border = 25 - 9 = ?
exercises.explanation: 25 - 9 = 16. Our check value. Each area comes from the same helper.

exercises.prompt: area(5) and area(3) must RETURN their results so we can subtract them.
exercises.explanation: Yes — returned values can be subtracted. A print-only helper couldn't be composed this way.
Define the helper, call it for both squares, subtract, show. Build the piece, then use it twice.

exercises.prompt: Which expression computes the border using the helper?
exercises.explanation: Subtract the inner area from the outer: area(5) - area(3). area(5-3) would wrongly compute area(2).

exercises.prompt: Code the helper and the composition. Arrange the lines.
exercises.explanation: Define area, then border = area(5) - area(3), then print. One helper, composed into the answer.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the border calculation using the helper twice:

def area(side):
    return side * side
border = area(5) ____ area(3)
print(border)
exercises.explanation: Subtract the inner area from the outer: 25 - 9 = 16.

exercises.prompt: Run it: prints 16. Hand said 16. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Matches. You decomposed the problem into one helper and composed the answer — real engineering!

exercises.prompt: Re-run with outer 10, inner 6: area(10) - area(6) = ?
exercises.explanation: 100 - 36 = 64. The same helper serves any sizes. Build once, reuse everywhere!
